free_tier.stated: No free tier. The German IPv6-only ladder starts at EX0DE, USD 1.11 a month for 256 MB and 20 GB; EX2DE is EUR 2.99 a month for 2 vCPU, 2 GB and 75 GB. Every rung is unmetered bandwidth on a 500 Mbps shared line and includes 5 IPv6 addresses.

retention.stated: billed monthly through triennially with 5, 10 and 20 percent discounts for the longer terms; no deletion grace period is printed

egress.terms: 'Unmetered' bandwidth on a 500 Mbps shared network line, for every rung of the IPv6-only ladder

interface_detail: OpenVZ containers per the store's own category listing ('OpenVZ' on every EX card), 5 IPv6 addresses per server, and a free IPv4-to-IPv6 SSH tunnel so an IPv4-only admin can reach the box. The vendor's knowledgebase also says the guest cannot reach IPv4 destinations at all.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6, or the vendor's IPv4-to-IPv6 SSH tunnel from an IPv4-only network

notes: Recorded as dead rather than as a cheap row because the purchase path does not work: every order link on the IPv6 page carries a pid that the store bounces to the bare storefront, and five of them were fetched individually with the same result. The prices also disagree between the marketing page (USD 1.11 to 11.18) and the store category (EUR 2.99 to 5.99 on monthly), which is a second signal that the page is stale. Two things are worth keeping if the line comes back: the free IPv4-to-IPv6 SSH tunnel is the only admin workaround for an IPv4-only operator found, and the guest cannot reach IPv4 destinations at all, which is stated plainly in the vendor's own FAQ. The EX range is OpenVZ, so the guest does not get its own kernel, which matters for WireGuard.
